items.why: 16.Rd1 pins Black's queen on d6 to the king on d8, so it is lost for a rook: 16...Nf5 17.Rxd6+ Nxd6 18.Qh4+ leaves White about eight pawns up. Quieter moves like 16.Ba4 or castling let the queen off the hook and are worth only about +3.5.

19...Bd4 pins White's queen on f2 to the king on g1, and the c5 pawn guards the bishop, so the queen is lost for a bishop: 20.Nd1 Bxf2+ 21.Nxf2 leaves Black about four pawns up. The natural 19...Bg7 is only level.
A quiet queen move with no check that threatens ...Qb2# and leaves White no defence. The forced mate follows.
A queen sacrifice: after Kxf7, Rxf6+ wins the black queen and exd4 takes the knight, leaving a winning pawn ending. The natural Rxf6 throws the win away.
A rook sacrifice that drags the queen onto g2, where Qxg2 is mate with the knight on e3 guarding it.
The queen takes the d2 rook with check. After 15.Kxd2 Bxb1 the bishop takes White's queen, so Black has won a rook and a queen for his queen: five points ahead.

items.why: 14...Nxe4 lets White take the g7 bishop and then the f8 rook, but 15.Bxg7 Nxd2 grabs White's queen, and after 16.Bxf8 Nb3+ 17.cxb3 Rxb3 Black stays about six pawns up. The alternative 14...Bxh6 is good, but more than a pawn weaker.
The queen sacrifice 22.Qf8+ forces 22...Rxf8, and 23.Rxf8# is a back-rank mate.
The bishop sacrifice on g6 uncovers the d-file. After 8...Kd7 9.Rd1+ Kc7 10.Rxd8, White wins Black's queen and comes out more than six pawns up.
The queen sacrifice on f7 drags the rook there with 15...Rxf7, and 16.Nxg6# is mate.
The rook takes on f2, and after 25.Qxf2 Rxf2 26.Rxa6 Rxd2+ 27.Rxb6 Rd1+ Black keeps a winning position, about six pawns up. The quieter 24...Be2 keeps only about half the advantage.
The bishop sacrifice 6.Bxf7+ Kxf7 7.Nxe5+ wins the pawn back and drags the black king into the open, leaving White close to three pawns up. Quiet moves like 6.Qd5 give it all away.
The knight sacrifice 7.Nxf7 Kxf7 8.Bg6+ is a trick: 8...Kxg6 9.Qxd8 wins the black queen. Retreating with 7.Ne4 would leave White worse.
The bishop check starts a king hunt: 9...Kd4 10.Qe4+ Kc5 11.Qc4+ Kb6 12.Qb4# is mate, exactly as played.
